slides.title: Tukey's Epistemological Decomposition: Data = Fit + Residual

solo.speaker: Dr. Nova (Senior Architect)
solo.title: Tukey's Epistemological Decomposition: Data = Fit + Residual

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova
turns.text: Tukey's Epistemological Decomposition: Data = Fit + Residual. Formalizing the empirical sample mathematically reveals that empirical risk only approximates true generalization risk when the i.i.d. assumption holds. When upstream sampling is biased, the empirical risk diverges asymptotically from true risk—no model tuning can fix that.

solo.contentHtml:
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Sample Formulation
$$\text{Data} = \text{Fit} + \text{Residual}$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Distribution Measure
$$\mathbf{y} = \hat{\mathbf{y}} + \mathbf{e}$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Risk Proxy
$$s_e^2 = \frac{1}{n - p} \sum_{i=1}^n e_i^2 = \frac{1}{n - p} \sum_{i=1}^n \left(y_i - \hat{y}_i\right)^2$$
◆
The core mathematical: principle unifying all exploratory data analysis is Tukey's additive decomposition: where: - $\hat{\mathbf{y}} = f(\mathbf{x})$ represents the smooth, low-dimensional structured signal (the "fit", such as median, regression spline, or cluster prototype).
▸
The sample residual: variance is given by: where $p$ is the effective degrees of freedom consumed by the fitting procedure.
⚡
To achieve resistance: against arbitrary leverage outliers, robust regression utilizes the Theil-Sen Estimator (Tukey, 1977), which calculates the median of all pairwise slopes: The Theil-Sen estimator has a finite-sample breakdown point of $\epsilon^* \approx 29.3\%$, meaning nearly a third of observations can be arbitrarily corrupted without destroying the slope estimate.
💡
EDA demands an: iterative alternating inspection: analysts model the fit, subtract it, and inspect the residuals $\mathbf{e}$ for systematic non-random structures (e.g., heteroscedasticity, periodicity, or multimodal sub-populations).

slides.title: Normality and Diagnostic Moment Testing

solo.speaker: Dr. Nova (Senior Architect)
solo.title: Normality and Diagnostic Moment Testing

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova
turns.text: Normality and Diagnostic Moment Testing. Formalizing the empirical sample mathematically reveals that empirical risk only approximates true generalization risk when the i.i.d. assumption holds. When upstream sampling is biased, the empirical risk diverges asymptotically from true risk—no model tuning can fix that.

solo.contentHtml:
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Sample Formulation
$$\sqrt{b_1} = \frac{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^3}{\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2\right)^{3/2}}, \quad b_2 = \frac{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^4}{\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2\right)^2}$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Distribution Measure
$$K^2 = Z_1(\sqrt{b_1})^2 + Z_2(b_2)^2 \sim \chi^2(2)$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Risk Proxy
$$\text{MAD} = \text{median}\left(|x_i - \text{median}(\mathbf{x})|\right)$$
◆
To evaluate whether: residuals or raw features conform to Gaussian assumptions, exploratory profiling utilizes the D'Agostino-Pearson Omnibus $K^2$ Test, combining standardized skewness $\sqrt{b_1}$ and kurtosis $b_2$: Under Gaussian assumptions, transformed statistics $Z_1(\sqrt{b_1})$ and $Z_2(b_2)$ are asymptotically standard normal $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, yielding the omnibus statistic: When $K^2$ exceeds critical values (e.g., $\chi_{0.95, 2}^2 = 5.991$), Gaussian assumptions are rejected, requiring non-parametric or robust order statistics.
▸
For scale estimation: under contaminated distributions, the Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) provides optimal $50\%$ breakdown resistance: where $\Phi^{-1}(0.75) \approx 0.6745$ is the 75th percentile of the standard normal distribution.

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova
turns.text: Empirical Case Study: The 1854 Broad Street Cholera Outbreak & Modern Telemetry. Systems collapse when models mistake collection artifacts for real-world signals. In ICU sepsis models, observation frequency became a confounder; in autonomous robotics, a 50-millisecond timestamp jitter causes a 1.4-meter bounding box dislocation at highway speeds.

solo.contentHtml:
◆
Snow's Cholera Map (London, 1854): Dr. John Snow rejected the prevailing *miasma theory* of airborne contagion through spatial EDA. By plotting cholera deaths on a map of Soho along with public water pump locations, the geographic clustering exposed that mortality centered around the Broad Street water pump. The physical removal of the pump handle immediately curtailed the epidemic—a historic triumph of exploratory data visualization driving causal intervention.
▸
Modern Server Telemetry (Datacenter Cluster): An engineering team observed sporadic latency spikes on production APIs. Aggregate summary metrics showed normal mean latency ($24\text{ ms}$). Exploratory visual quantile heatmaps revealed a severe bimodal subpopulation: $99\%$ of requests took $12\text{ ms}$, but requests routed to a specific misconfigured container pool took $2,400\text{ ms}$. Summary statistics had masked the degradation entirely.

📐 Mathematical Formulation Distribution Measure
$$\sigma_{\text{total}}^2 = \sum_{k=1}^K p_k \sigma_k^2 + \sum_{k=1}^K p_k (\mu_k - \bar{\mu})^2$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Risk Proxy
$$\eta^2 = \frac{\text{Var}(\mathbb{E}[Y \mid G])}{\text{Var}(Y)} = \frac{\sum_{k=1}^K p_k (\mu_k - \bar{\mu})^2}{\sigma_{\text{total}}^2}$$

◆
When analyzing heterogeneous: datasets partitioned across categorical groups $G \in \{1, \dots, K\}$, the global variance decomposes into within-group and between-group components: where $p_k = \frac{n_k}{n}$ is the group proportion, $\mu_k$ is the group conditional mean, and $\sigma_k^2$ is the group conditional variance.
▸

tip "Industrial Best: Practice: Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) for Dispersion" When measuring variance in non-Gaussian or outlier-contaminated datasets, replace standard deviation with Median Absolute Deviation (MAD): Multiply by the asymptotic consistency factor $1.4826$ to yield an unbiased estimator of $\sigma$ for normally distributed inliers that is immune to extreme outliers up to a 50% breakdown point (Tukey, 1977).

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova
turns.text: Empirical Case Study: Financial Fraud and Sensor Tail Heaviness. Systems collapse when models mistake collection artifacts for real-world signals. In ICU sepsis models, observation frequency became a confounder; in autonomous robotics, a 50-millisecond timestamp jitter causes a 1.4-meter bounding box dislocation at highway speeds.

solo.contentHtml:
◆
High-Frequency Trading Network Latency: A proprietary trading firm upgraded network switches across three server clusters. Mean round-trip latency improved marginally from $18\text{ µs}$ to $16\text{ µs}$. However, trading models experienced catastrophic execution misses. Moment analysis revealed that while the mean dropped, excess kurtosis skyrocketed from $G_2 = 1.2$ to $G_2 = 48.7$: micro-burst buffer congestion generated massive 99.9th percentile outlier packets ($2,500\text{ µs}$) that bankrupted algorithmic orders. The firm rolled back the switch firmware after diagnosing kurtosis inflation.
▸
Subscription SaaS Customer Revenue Heterogeneity: A SaaS provider analyzed monthly revenue per user ($n=50,000$). The global variance was massive ($\sigma^2 = \$450,000$). Using Eve's Law, data engineers stratified users by plan tier (Enterprise, Professional, Starter). Between-group variance accounted for $89.2\%$ of the total variance ($\eta^2 = 0.892$), while within-group variance for Starter users had a Gini coefficient of only $0.12$. Modeling cohorts independently reduced predictive revenue forecast error by $74\%$.

In ICU sepsis models, observation frequency became a confounder; in autonomous robotics, a 50-millisecond timestamp jitter causes a 1.4-meter bounding box dislocation at highway speeds.

solo.contentHtml:
◆
Autonomous Vehicle LiDAR-Radar Calibration Failure: During rainy highway trials, an autonomous vehicle perceived phantom obstacles. Aggregate logging showed a high Pearson correlation ($r = 0.91$) between LiDAR point counts and Radar reflectivity. However, exploratory bivariate scatterplots revealed an extreme outlier cluster: under wet road glare, LiDAR suffered total backscatter absorption ($x \approx 0$), while Radar detected ground spray ($y \approx 4,000$). However, replacing the scatterplot with a LOWESS-smoothed hexbin plot exposed a sharp non-linear threshold: CPU stayed flat at $15\%$ until connections reached $1,024$, at which point lock contention triggered an exponential wall to $100\%$. The non-linear relationship was invisible to summary correlation.

slides.title: Empirical Case Study: Healthcare Records & Silent Feature Death

solo.speaker: Dr. Nova (Senior Architect)
solo.title: Empirical Case Study: Healthcare Records & Silent Feature Death

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova
turns.text: Empirical Case Study: Healthcare Records & Silent Feature Death. Systems collapse when models mistake collection artifacts for real-world signals. In ICU sepsis models, observation frequency became a confounder; in autonomous robotics, a 50-millisecond timestamp jitter causes a 1.4-meter bounding box dislocation at highway speeds.

solo.contentHtml:
◆
Intensive Care Clinical EHR Schema Drift: An academic hospital deployed a predictive sepsis alert engine. Over a six-month period, false-negative sepsis alerts rose by $310\%$. Root-cause EDA revealed that a software update to the bedside monitor system renamed systolic_bp_arterial to art_bp_sys. The pipeline silently ingested the newly missing column as nulls and imputed the median ($120\text{ mmHg}$). An automated profiling gate checking missingness thresholds would have flagged the $100\%$ null spike at $t=0$, preventing catastrophic patient monitoring failure.
▸
E-Commerce Fraud Classification Leaks: A fraud detection startup observed $99.9\%$ test ROC-AUC on a synthesized benchmark. Automated profiling flagged a quasi-identifier session_hash with $100\%$ unique cardinality that exhibited a Cramér's $V = 0.99$ with the fraud label: the transaction logging system included a timestamp suffix only on flagged sessions. Automated cardinality alerts eliminated the data leakage before production deployment.

solo.speaker: Dr. Nova (Senior Architect)
solo.title: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) & The Biplot Geometry

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova
turns.text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) & The Biplot Geometry. Formalizing the empirical sample mathematically reveals that empirical risk only approximates true generalization risk when the i.i.d. assumption holds. When upstream sampling is biased, the empirical risk diverges asymptotically from true risk—no model tuning can fix that.

solo.contentHtml:
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Sample Formulation
$$\max_{\mathbf{v}_1} \frac{1}{n} \mathbf{v}_1^\top \mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{X} \mathbf{v}_1 \quad \text{subject to } \mathbf{v}_1^\top \mathbf{v}_1 = 1$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Distribution Measure
$$\mathbf{S} = \frac{1}{n - 1} \mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{X} = \mathbf{V} \boldsymbol{\Lambda} \mathbf{V}^\top$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Risk Proxy
$$\text{EVR}_j = \frac{\lambda_j}{\sum_{m=1}^d \lambda_m}$$
◆
Given centered data: matrix $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$ ($\frac{1}{n} \mathbf{1}^\top \mathbf{X} = \mathbf{0}$), PCA seeks an orthogonal projection matrix $\mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times k}$ ($k \ll d$) maximizing projected variance (Jolliffe, 2016): The solution corresponds to the eigendecomposition of sample covariance matrix $\mathbf{S}$: where $\boldsymbol{\Lambda} = \text{diag}(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_d)$ with eigenvalues sorted $\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_d \ge 0$.

solo.speaker: Dr. Nova (Senior Architect)

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova

Formalizing the empirical sample mathematically reveals that empirical risk only approximates true generalization risk when the i.i.d. assumption holds. solo.contentHtml:
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Sample Formulation
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{UMAP}} = \sum_{i \neq j} \left( p_{ij} \log \frac{p_{ij}}{q_{ij}} + (1 - p_{ij}) \log \frac{1 - p_{ij}}{1 - q_{ij}} \right)$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Distribution Measure
$$s(i) = \frac{b(i) - a(i)}{\max(a(i), b(i))} \in [-1, 1]$$
◆
UMAP models the: manifold using fuzzy simplicial sets and fuzzy set cross-entropy (McInnes, 2018): Unlike t-SNE, the second term penalizes non-neighbors being placed close together, preserving global manifold topology much more faithfully.

solo.speaker: Dr. Nova (Senior Architect)

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova
turns.text: Spurious Correlation in Non-Stationary Time Series. Formalizing the empirical sample mathematically reveals that empirical risk only approximates true generalization risk when the i.i.d. assumption holds. When upstream sampling is biased, the empirical risk diverges asymptotically from true risk—no model tuning can fix that.

solo.contentHtml:
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Sample Formulation
$$X_t = X_{t-1} + \epsilon_{1t}, \quad \epsilon_{1t} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_1^2)$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Distribution Measure
$$Y_t = Y_{t-1} + \epsilon_{2t}, \quad \epsilon_{2t} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_2^2)$$
📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Risk Proxy
$$\Delta X_t = \alpha + \beta t + \gamma X_{t-1} + \sum_{i=1}^p \delta_i \Delta X_{t-i} + e_t$$
◆
Udny Yule (Yule,: 1926) proved that computing correlation coefficients between non-stationary integrated time series $I(1)$ produces massive, statistically significant correlations even when the underlying generating processes are completely independent Brownian motions: with $\mathbb{E}[\epsilon_{1t} \epsilon_{2s}] = 0$ for all $t, s$.
▸
As sample duration: $T \to \infty$, the sample correlation coefficient $r_{XY}$ does not converge in probability to zero ($r \not\xrightarrow{p} 0$).
⚡
Instead, it follows: a non-degenerate random variable distribution with high probability of $|r| > 0.80$.

📐 Mathematical Formulation Empirical Sample Formulation
$$\text{Cov}(A, B \mid C = 1) < 0$$

$$\text{OR}(A, B \mid C = 1) = \frac{\Pr(A=1, B=1 \mid C=1) \Pr(A=0, B=0 \mid C=1)}{\Pr(A=1, B=0 \mid C=1) \Pr(A=0, B=1 \mid C=1)} < 1$$
◆
Berkson's Fallacy (Berkson,: 1946) occurs when selecting or conditioning on a common effect variable (a collider $C$) induces a spurious negative association between two independent causes $A$ and $B$.

turns.speaker: Dr. Nova

In ICU sepsis models, observation frequency became a confounder; in autonomous robotics, a 50-millisecond timestamp jitter causes a 1.4-meter bounding box dislocation at highway speeds.

solo.contentHtml:
◆
Berkson's Paradox in Medical Trials: A clinical study on diabetes and kidney failure among hospitalized patients found that diabetic patients had a lower risk of acute kidney failure ($\text{OR} = 0.65$). Clinicians hypothesized that diabetic medication was nephroprotective. In reality, hospitalization was a common collider: patients with kidney disease were admitted immediately; diabetic patients were also admitted frequently. Among admitted non-diabetics, acute kidney failure was vastly higher because severe trauma or sepsis was required to trigger admission. In the outpatient population, diabetes was strongly nephrotoxic ($\text{OR} = 2.4$).
▸

Engineers observed a strong positive correlation between average ambient cabin temperature and brake pad failure rate. Team members speculated that heat degraded hydraulic brake fluid. When data was stratified by geographic state, the correlation vanished: vehicles in mountainous Colorado and California drove on steep descents with prolonged braking during hot summer vacation months. The apparent temperature link was pure spatial confounding.
